title: The derivative as the slope of a curve
examples: What is a derivative in simple words?

explain.say: Picture throwing a ball straight up. This curve shows its height as time goes on. Look at the yellow mark: the curve is steep here, because the ball rises fast. Steepness is called slope, and the derivative is simply the slope at one moment.

explain.say: But a curve bends, so how can one point have a slope? Let us zoom in. See how a tiny piece looks almost straight? The slope of that straight bit is the derivative at that point.

explain.say: Now the cyan mark at the top. For one instant the ball stops going up and has not started down. The curve is flat, so the slope, the derivative, is zero. Can you see why the top is flat?

explain.say: Look at the purple mark. The curve goes down now, so the slope is negative. The ball is falling, and the derivative tells you how fast. Going up means positive, going down means negative.

explain.say: Well done! You just read a derivative with your eyes: steep means fast change, flat means no change. Engineers use this every day, from rocket launches in India to the speed your phone's map shows you.

faq.a: A derivative is the slope of a curve at one point. It tells you how fast one thing changes as another changes, like height changing with time.

faq.q: Why is the slope zero at the top?
faq.a: At the very top the curve stops going up and has not started going down, so for one instant it is flat. A flat line has slope zero.
asks: Why is the derivative zero at a maximum?

faq.q: What does a negative derivative mean?
faq.a: It means the quantity is going down as x increases. For a falling ball, a negative derivative of height means it is losing height.
asks: What does a negative slope mean?

faq.a: A tangent line just touches the curve at one point and has the same slope as the curve there. Zoom in far enough and the curve looks like its tangent.
asks: What is a tangent to a curve?

faq.q: How do you write a derivative?
faq.a: We write dy by dx, or f dash of x. Both mean the rate at which y changes as x changes.

facts: The derivative of a function at a point equals the slope of the tangent line to its graph at that point.
The notation dy/dx comes from Gottfried Leibniz; the dash notation f′(x) was popularised by Joseph-Louis Lagrange.

quiz.say: At the very top of a ball's flight, what is the derivative of its height?
quiz.show: At the very top of a ball's flight, what is the derivative of its height?
quiz.why: At the top the height curve is flat for an instant, so its slope is zero.

wrong.0: The height is biggest at the top, but its rate of change is zero.
wrong.1: The slope turns negative only after the top, as the ball falls.

quiz.say: A height curve is going down. Its derivative is…
quiz.show: A height curve is going down. Its derivative is…
quiz.why: A curve going down has a negative slope.

wrong.1: A positive slope means going up.
wrong.2: Zero slope means flat, not going down.
